title: Flight booking API in Express
idea: The flight booking API exposes bookings and seat choices as REST resources: the controller validates, the service decides in a transaction, the repository runs SQL.

analogy.text: An airport check-in desk. The agent checks your passport, the airline system decides, and the baggage belt only moves bags.
analogy.breaks: A desk agent can bend rules; the repository never decides anything.

points: A hold POSTs to the flight's `bookings` path: 201, or 409 when sold out.
Every hold needs an Idempotency-Key header; a replay returns the same PNR with 200.
`zod` rejects bad bodies with 400 before the service runs.
A seat clash surfaces as Postgres `23505`; the service maps it to 409.

code.title: Layered Express app
code.caption: Repository, service, controllers and error mapping in one file on a real PostgreSQL. Seat existence and cabin checks are left out to keep it short.

walk.text: Demo schema: fare counts, bookings with a unique key, and one seat per flight.
A fixed demo clock; `tx` wraps each service call in one transaction.
Repository: plain SQL, including the conditional UPDATE that takes seats from the fare.
Service `hold`: replay a known key, else 404, 409, or a new HELD booking.
Service `seat`: a unique violation becomes 409 SEAT_TAKEN.
Controllers demand the key and parse bodies and params with `zod`; Express 5 forwards async throws.
One error middleware maps validation, bad JSON, domain and duplicate-key errors to status codes.

pitfalls: Never call the payment provider inside an open transaction; the fare row stays locked.
Two requests with one new key can both miss the lookup; UNIQUE must catch it.
Do not return 500 for a taken seat; 409 tells the client to reload the map.

quiz.q: What status does the third POST, with key k-2, print?
quiz.why: k-2 is a new key, so it is not a replay. Two seats were loaded and PNR-1 took both, so the conditional UPDATE matches no row: SOLD_OUT, 409.

takeaway: Validate in the controller, decide in one transaction, retry safely with Idempotency-Key.

starters: Where should the payment call go in the payment endpoint?
Should seat selection need an Idempotency-Key too?
How would the search endpoint stay fast under heavy traffic?
